propertyTaxRate.note: Tax Foundation Table 2 (Census ACS 2024 5-year): NY 1.30% (2023: 1.31%). File 1.72% is 0.42 pp high; statewide median is pulled down by NYC's low effective rates, so an upstate-only model would run higher, but the file figure has no current source.

programs.name: Alternative Veterans Property Tax Exemption

survivingSpouse.quote: A qualifying owner for the alternative exemption includes a veteran of a defined period of war, the recipient of an expeditionary medal, the spouse of the veteran or the surviving spouse who has not remarried.

wartimeRequired.quote: Available only on residential property of a veteran who has served during a designated time of war.

tiers.correct: 15% wartime (cap $12,000 basic), +10% combat zone (cap $8,000), + half of disability rating (cap $40,000); locality may reduce to $6,000/$4,000/$20,000 or raise in steps to $75,000/$50,000/$250,000; caps x equalization rate
tiers.quote: Reduced maximums 6,000 4,000 20,000 ... Basic maximums 12,000 8,000 40,000 ... Increased maximums 15,000 10,000 50,000

exemptionValue.quote: Each of these reductions is subject to maximum limits set by the local community. Check with your assessor to determine the maximum exemption limits in your community.

programs.effectiveChanges: None to the percentage/cap schedule for TY2026 or TY2027. Form RP-458-a and RP-458-a-I were reissued 9/26 to fold in the 458-a(11) full exemption (Lines 8 and 10).
programs.note: The $40,000 market-equivalent is a modeling choice, not a statutory figure; it is plausible for a 100% rated wartime veteran at basic caps ($12,000 + $40,000 of assessed value x equalization) but cannot be verified as a single number. The disability component is 50% of the rating applied to assessed value, so it scales with rating; a tiers[] array keyed to rating would model it better than a flat value.

programs.name: Cold War Veterans Property Tax Exemption

summary.correct: Local option (RPTL 458-b) for veterans who served Sept 2, 1945 to Dec 26, 1991 with no wartime service: 10% or 15% of assessed value (basic caps $8,000 / $12,000, local range $4,000 to $48,000 / $6,000 to $72,000), for 10 years unless the locality removes the limit, plus one-half of the VA disability rating off assessed value (basic cap $40,000, up to $240,000) with no time limit. Cannot be combined with the alternative exemption.
summary.quote: 10 or 15% of the assessed value to veterans who served during the Cold War, depending on the community. This exemption may only be granted for 10 years, except where a county, city, town village, or school district has opted to remove the 10-year limit.

survivingSpouse.quote: A qualifying owner for the exemption includes a veteran of the Cold War, the spouse of such veteran, or the unremarried surviving spouse.

tiers.correct: 10%/15% capped $8,000/$12,000 basic (local schedule $4,000-$48,000 / $6,000-$72,000); disability component half of rating capped $40,000 basic (up to $240,000)

wartimeRequired.quote: The veteran must have served on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces between September 2, 1945, and December 26, 1991

programs.note: Row had an empty summary. A rated veteran takes either this or the alternative exemption, not both; most rated veterans with wartime/expeditionary service are better off under 458-a.

programs.name: Eligible Funds Veterans Property Tax Exemption

exemptionValue.quote: equal to the amount of eligible funds used to purchase the home, generally up to a maximum of $7,500.

survivingSpouse.quote: The unremarried surviving spouse of a veteran, who is also a veteran, may also receive the veterans' exemption of the deceased spouse.

details.current: Specially adapted housing grants get 100% exemption.
details.quote: Section 458 subdivision three provides a total exemption from general municipal and school taxes, and special district charges to certain seriously disabled veterans who are eligible for or who have received and used monies granted by the federal government to acquire specially adapted housing

programs.note: The $7,500 cap is on assessed value and only to the extent eligible funds (pension, bonus, insurance, POW compensation) were actually used in the purchase; it cannot be stacked with the alternative or Cold War exemption on the same parcel. Should not be scored for a rated veteran by default; the SAH-grant total exemption (RPTL 458(3)) is the only part that reliably reaches a rated veteran's home and it is a separate population (SAH recipients).

programs.name: Full Exemption for 100% P&T Disabled Veterans (RPTL 458-a(11), NEW 2026)

type.quote: At local option, a county, city, town, village, or school district may provide a full exemption from real property taxes, special ad valorem levies, and special assessments on the primary residence of a veteran who has a permanent and total disability as a result of military service.

ptRequired.quote: The documentation must specifically state the veteran is considered to be permanently and totally disabled

wartimeRequired.quote: To be eligible for the full exemption, the veteran must meet all eligibility requirements of the alternative veterans exemption

survivingSpouse.quote: A qualifying owner for the alternative exemption includes a veteran of a defined period of war, the recipient of an expeditionary medal, the spouse of the veteran or the surviving spouse who has not remarried.

localOption.quote: subdivision 11 now provides a full exemption, at local option, to qualifying veterans

effectiveRoll.current: taxable status dates on or after Oct 1, 2026
effectiveRoll.quote: this exemption will apply to assessment rolls based on taxable status dates occurring on or after October 1, 2026

programs.effectiveChanges: First reaches rolls with taxable status dates on/after Oct 1, 2026, only where adopted: for March 1 towns that is the 2027 roll (2027-28 school bill, Jan 2028 town/county bill). Localities adopt by local law or resolution and must notify the Dept of Veterans' Services within 30 days (statute text read on nysenate.gov, which blocks automated checks). Whether the TDIU-based P&T letter qualifies is still not addressed in the 9/26 instructions.
programs.note: Row summary and note already describe the Feb 2026 mandatory-then-local-option sequence correctly. One wording caveat: the file cites 'L.2026 ch.59 Part EE'; the Tax Department's own notice identifies the amendment as 'bill number S.9009-C Part EE' of the 2026-27 budget and does not print a chapter number, so the chapter citation is unverified. Eligibility rides on the alternative exemption, so wartime or expeditionary-medal service is required, which the row does not flag (wartimeRequired should be true). Row name says '100% P&T'; the standard is VA 'permanently and totally disabled', not literally 100%.
